acceptedAnswer.text: Conversion rate optimisation is the work of getting more of your existing visitors to buy or enquire, by finding where they drop off and testing changes to the pages, checkout and forms they use.

mainEntity.name: How does conversion optimisation work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We start from your funnel data and how visitors actually behave, rank possible changes by what the leak costs and how easy the fix is, test them one at a time, and keep only what beats the current page.
Scoped after a call, based on your traffic, the pages in scope and how many tests you want run. We quote once we have seen your funnel data. Any ad spend stays with the platforms and outside our fee.
No. Some tests win and some do not, so we cannot promise an uplift. We commit to a structured process, tests run long enough to trust, and honest reporting.

D2C stores whose website gets traffic but does not convert, and B2B and education sites that lose enquiries at the landing page or the form. Not only D2C. We work with D2C, B2B and education brands, and set the work up differently for each: D2C on contribution margin and repeat purchase, B2B on the cost of a qualified lead, education on enquiries, visits and admissions.

leaks.note: Screens are illustrative recreations of each platform's interface, not client data. Platform names and logos belong to their owners.
leaks.lede: You pay to bring visitors in, then lose most of them. Each stage below is where they leave, and the CRO work that keeps them.

stages.breaks: Guessing which page needs a redesign.
stages.why: Redesigns based on opinion often fix the wrong page. The biggest leak is usually somewhere less obvious.
stages.does: We analyse funnel steps and session behaviour to find where visitors drop off, and rank the leaks by how much they cost.

stages.breaks: A page that describes the product but does not answer doubts.
stages.why: Visitors leave when price, delivery, returns, proof or fit are not clear near the decision.
stages.does: We rework key pages so the questions a visitor has are answered where they arise, with clear proof and one obvious next step.

stages.breaks: A long checkout with surprises at the end.
stages.why: Extra steps, forced sign-ups and unexpected costs make people abandon a purchase they had already decided on.
stages.does: We simplify the cart and checkout, including the payment options Indian shoppers expect such as UPI and cash on delivery, and remove friction.

stages.breaks: Long forms that ask for everything at once.
stages.why: Most enquiries start on a phone. Every extra field costs you a lead who was already interested.
stages.does: We test shorter forms, clearer calls to action and options like WhatsApp, so more interested visitors become leads.

stages.breaks: Changing pages and hoping the numbers improve.
stages.why: Without a test you cannot tell whether a change helped, or whether sales rose for another reason.
stages.does: We run controlled tests on the changes worth making and keep only what beats the current page, so the gains are real.
